forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8280'
+title: 'MTP: stay faster than plain under CPU load (adaptive block size / plain fallback, fewer host syncs)'
+---
+Final verification of stable 148f227e at load average 10–14 showed MTP losing to plain on some turns (ChatSession edit turn 34.6 vs 52.3 tok/s; guided JSON 11.8 vs 14.3) while other turns kept 1.4–1.7x. MTP does host syncs every round (verify readback, plus one per chained step for the pMin gate), so CPU contention costs it more than plain. The ACP SWE-bench run executes CPU-heavy work (django test runs, code-context index, other sessions' builds) next to generation, so this matters in production.
+
+Wait for data first: the quiet-machine rerun of the two failed benchmarks, mtpsmoke1 telemetry (tok/s per call + bench/load.mtpsmoke1.log in FoundationModelsACPAgent), and the SWE-bench-scale benchmark (^task 01M641KG6YT4FXK19NRJ2TNZPN).
+
+- [ ] Quantify: MTP/plain ratio vs load average (from the telemetry and a controlled run with a synthetic CPU load, e.g. N busy threads).
+- [ ] If MTP falls below plain under load: measure per-round host-sync time vs GPU time; cut syncs (batch the pMin check into the verify readback, async eval of the seed probability).
+- [ ] Adaptive policy: track emitted tokens per second of speculative rounds vs a periodic plain estimate (or round latency vs acceptance) and lower the block size or pause speculation when it isn't paying; resume when it is. Output must stay identical (greedy) / distribution-preserving (sampled), and cache/drafter state must stay consistent when pausing/resuming.
+- [ ] Release guards at quiet load stay ≥ current; under synthetic load MTP ≥ plain.
+
+#mtp #perf
\ No newline at end of file

+#mtp #perf
+
+## Review Findings (2026-10-29 11:40)
+
+> Scope: `review sha ed863693~1..ed863693` — reviewed the diffs only — lines this change added or modified. 15 file(s) reviewed, 2 not reviewed.
+
+> 2 file(s) not reviewed — no validator matched:
+> - `.kanban/tasks/01M642KXE2WG006RAY4TDJ3WAA.jsonl` — no validator matches this file
+> - `.kanban/tasks/01M642KXE2WG006RAY4TDJ3WAA.md` — no validator matches this file
+
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXGuidedGeneration/GuidedSpeculation.swift:253` `swift/preconditions` — When a paused forward returns no hidden row, the speculation ends through `stoodDown = true` with no log and no recorded reason. The end of the stream is then silent, and the `GuidedGenerationDiagnosticSink` shows nothing about why speculation stopped. Record why the speculation stopped, for example by setting a stand-down reason that the completion information reports, or by pairing the branch with `assertionFailure` and a production log, as the rule requires for an unexpected but recoverable condition.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/MTPAdaptiveSpeculation.swift:416` `code-hygiene/magic-numbers-swift` — Magic numbers should be replaced by named constants.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/MTPAdaptiveSpeculation.swift:447` `code-hygiene/magic-numbers-swift` — Magic numbers should be replaced by named constants.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/MTPSpeculativeTokenIterator.swift:1518` `duplication/duplication` — `nextGuardedPlainToken` repeats the three-line buffer reset that `next()` already performs before a speculation round. A later change to how the pending buffer is cleared would have to be made in both places. Move the three resets into one private method, such as `resetPendingBuffer()`, and call it from both `next()` and `nextGuardedPlainToken()`.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/MTPSpeculativeTokenIterator.swift:1560` `duplication/duplication` — `feedPlainStep` repeats the forward-feed sequence of `passthroughStep`: build the state with the emit flag, call `mainModel` on the one-token input, commit the processed tokens, sample from the logits, apply the KV cache plan, and start evaluation. The copies differ only in the input token shape, whether the snapshot key is cleared, and whether shared-KV reconciliation runs. Those differences are what a shared helper should take as parameters, so the two can drift apart. Extract one private helper that takes the token array, and an optional flag for the shared-KV reconciliation.
